# HoloVinyl

Objects select music; hand gestures control playback.

- Dates: 2025
- Status: Computer vision prototype
- Areas: Software engineering; AI / ML
- Stack: Python · YOLO11 · MediaPipe · Spotify
- Topics: Python; Computer Vision; Gesture UI; Interfaces; Music
- Public case study: https://mgiorgetti.com/project_details/project-holovinyl.html

## Problem

A physical music interface needs to recognize an object consistently and translate hand gestures into intentional playback controls.

## Contribution

Solo computer-vision prototype joining object recognition, hand tracking, object-to-music configuration and Spotify playback.

## Technical approach and public case study

A camera-based music interface: objects select Spotify tracks, and hand gestures control playback.

- Solo project

- Python · YOLO11 · MediaPipe

- Working prototype

The prototype recognizing a card in the camera feed.

### Object recognition and hand tracking

#### Object-to-music mapping

A fine-tuned YOLO11 model recognizes the objects in front of the camera. Each class maps to a Spotify source; several steady detections are required before an object becomes active.

#### Point and pinch controls

MediaPipe tracks the hand over the camera view. Point at a playback control and pinch to click it. ArUco markers align the physical surface with the interface.

### Objects and gestures controlling music

### Train a new object

Capture photos, train the detector, and assign music from the same interface.

- Capture Name the object and take five photos.

- Train Background removal produces labels for fine-tuning the detector.

- Map Assign the recognised class a Spotify track, album, or playlist.

Several recognised objects in the live camera feed.

The class-mapping screen links objects with music.

### Recognising an unfamiliar object

An optional workflow uses Moondream to describe an object and DeepSeek to turn that description into a music query. These models run locally; Spotify playback requires a network connection.

## Results and limitations

The case study provides a working-prototype demonstration. Optional object-description and music-query models run locally; Spotify playback still requires a network connection. No recognition-accuracy benchmark is published.
